post.summary:
Login via domain id + PIN. Resolves the account and issues a multi-role token.
    Named adult and not father because the same endpoint logs in a teacher account:
its id is likewise an Adult id, and the response then names Creator instead of
Supervisor. An existing account is not granted an additional role in the process
(see AccountService), so a teacher does not become a supervisor by logging in.
Child login via id + PIN. Resolves the account and issues a role token.
Canonical, account-centric login: a single token that carries all roles of the account (e.g. Creator + Supervisor). `role` in the response is the primary tier (Supervisor or Student) for UI routing.

get.summary: Returns the current identity from the token (account, all roles, fid/cid).

patch.summary:
Self-management of the account itself: display name, email and PIN.

     Lives under auth/… and not under a tier because it belongs to none – the same person
operates it from any role (the documented exception in CLAUDE.md). Previously this only worked via
supervisor/adults/{id}, and thus not at all for a teacher account: it lacks the
Supervisor role, so it couldn't change its own PIN.
     Identity hangs off two rows: the Adult row carries the domain name (it appears
as the author on exercises), the Account the login. Only the domain row is written
here; Task AccountService.MirrorAsync(Adult adult, CancellationToken ct) pulls the account along –
the same single place that supervisor/adults/{id} and supervisor/children/{id} use.
     Adults only. A child does not change its own name and PIN: the PIN is the
access the father grants, and a child that changed it would have escaped supervision.

post.summary: Capture a remark. Only the text is mandatory; author and role come from the token, the context from the widget. The response carries the id – it's the key used to later redeem the question in Claude Code.

get.summary:
List remarks. `mine=true` restricts to one's own – that's the query behind the
    list in the widget; without the filter a supervisor would also see the child's.
    scope=all lifts the account boundary – that's the view of the follow-up skill that
collects remarks from all test accounts. Allowed if bool RemarksController.MayReadAllAccounts holds
(switch Remarks:GlobalRead, on in development), otherwise 403. Deliberately an
explicit parameter: the default must stay narrow, otherwise the list in the widget would
suddenly show entries from other accounts. mine=true always wins.

A single remark – the entry point of the skill for "Answer question 123".
    An admin accesses this without scope=all: targeting a single id is exactly the
break-glass case, and a parameter you'd always have to send along would just be noise.

patch.summary:
Change a remark – text/categorization/status and the return channel (`answer`). PATCH semantics:
`null` leaves the value as is, clearing happens only via the `clear…` switches.

delete.summary:
Delete a remark.
    Deliberately narrow, even with GlobalRead switched on: the switch is called "global
read" and means exactly that. Answering and commenting across account boundaries is the point of
the feature; discarding another account's observation is not. An admin may still do it
(break-glass).

get.summary: The history of a remark, oldest first – a case reads chronologically, unlike the list of remarks (newest first).

post.summary:
Add an entry to the history.

An entry from Claude leaves the status untouched: it reports, it doesn't follow up. Otherwise every
implementation note would reopen its own remark.

post.summary:
"Different image" for a card. Deliberately addressed here and not at the child: which carrier
    holds the pick – the exercise-local override or the store vocabulary – only follows from the
    specificity cascade that only the server knows. The client only has the card in front of it.
    The rejected image never comes up again for this carrier. If there is no alternative, everything
stays unchanged (409 media_no_alternative) instead of leaving the card without an image.
    The endpoint hands out an image and therefore carries the same guards as the playback
itself: only the playable plan, only cards of this session, and only where the card actually shows an
image. Without the last guard it would be the hole in the anti-cheat rule – on a typed
stage it would deliver image and alt text and thereby the meaning of exactly the word that is
supposed to be typed ((string? Hint, int? AnswerLength, string? Reveal, IReadOnlyList<string>? Choices, string? AudioUrl, string? ImageUrl, string? ImageAlt) PositionPlayService.CardFacets(IReadOnlyList<ContentItem> items, ContentItem item, IExerciseType type, int stage, bool typed) deliberately withholds both there).

bool PlanPosition.RequireTypedTest. The server cursor then advances one card
and returns the next one right away. In PlayMode.Info no feedback flows (204).

That's why they are stored as int in the DB (not as a string like the other enums) and must never be renumbered – new levels are only appended at the end. Allowed values: Everyone, Teen, Mature.

CreateClozeDto.description: Input for creating a cloze. `Key` must be unique; at least one gap.

CreateCreatorProfileDto.description: Input for creating a profile. Only `Name` is required – everything else narrows the fit.

CreateEntryDto.description: Input for entering a subject on a weekday.

CreateInterestTagDto.description:
Creating a tag. The `Slug` may be omitted – it is then derived from the `Label`.
If the slug already exists, the endpoint returns the existing entry (idempotent).

CreateKeyResultRequest.description: Creation of a key result (scope + metric + target value + optional title).

CreateMediaAssetDto.description:
Creating an asset. `Key` may stay empty – the server then forms a unique slug from
the description. `Tags` (slugs) are linked create-if-missing; `Variants` can be
supplied right away or added individually later.

CreateMediaVariantDto.description: Creating a variant. (Purpose, format) is unique per asset.

CreateObjectiveRequest.description: Creation of an objective; key results can be supplied inline.

CreatePlanDto.description: Input for creating an empty study plan container.

exerciseId.description: The catalog exercise to assign; must be executable (execute permission or public).

order.description: Position within the plan; `null` = append at the end.

stage.description: Query form; `null` = inherits the exercise default (resolved only when played).

itemCount.description: Items per run; `null` = inherits the exercise default.

oneOf.description: Which part of the content (see ItemScope); `null` = all.
Goal cadence (see GoalCadence); `null` = no mandatory goal.

requireTypedTest.description: As in PositionResponse; `null` = inherits the exercise default.

useLeitner.description: As in PositionResponse; `null` = inherits the exercise default.

boxIntervalDays.description: Review intervals per box; `null` = method default.

stageSchedule.description: Stage schedule per box; `null` = method default.

pointsGoalMet.description: Points when the goal is met; `null` = 20.

penaltyCoins.description: Coin penalty for a missed mandatory goal; `null` = 0 (pure reward, opt-in).

newContentPoints.description: Points for new content; `null` = the exercise's bonus suggestion, otherwise 10.

comboThreshold.description: Combo threshold; `null` = the exercise's bonus suggestion, otherwise 5.

comboBonusPoints.description: Combo bonus; `null` = the exercise's bonus suggestion, otherwise 5.

speedThresholdSeconds.description: Time limit for "fast"; `null` = the exercise's bonus suggestion, otherwise 0 (off).

speedBonusPoints.description: Bonus per fast answer; `null` = the exercise's bonus suggestion, otherwise 0.

oneOf.description: Origin; defaults to RemarkCommentAuthor.Human if omitted.

CreateRemarkCommentDto.description:
Add a comment to the thread.
Deliberate side effect: A RemarkCommentAuthor.Human comment on a resolved or
dismissed remark pulls it back to RemarkStatus.Open – so the follow-up skill surfaces it
again on its next run. A RemarkCommentAuthor.Assistant comment leaves the state
untouched; it reports, it does not ask back.

oneOf.description: Optional categorization; defaults to RemarkCategory.Unspecified if omitted (the skill fills it in later).

parentRemarkId.description: Optional reference to the remark this one arose from (set by the skill, not the widget).

CreateRemarkDto.description: Capture a new remark. Only the text is required – everything else comes from the widget or stays empty.

CreateSeriesUnitDto.description: Input for creating a unit; without `OrderIndex` it is appended at the end.

CreateShopArticleDto.description: Input for creating a catalog article.

CreateShopListingDto.description: Input for creating a listing for an article.

CreateTagDto.description: Input for creating a child-scoped tag.

name.description: Display name – appears as the author on their exercises.

pin.description: Login PIN. Empty = the account cannot (yet) log in.

CreateTeacherDto.description: Input for teacher registration: an account that exclusively creates content.

CreateTextbookSeriesDto.description:
Input for creating a series. The slug is derived from the name; an already existing series
is returned instead of duplicated (idempotent).

CreateVocabTagDto.description: Input for creating a child-neutral vocabulary tag.

CreateVocabularyDto.description:
Creating a vocabulary entry. "Simple" only needs `Word` (+ languages): `Key` may stay
empty (the server generates a unique slug), `Translation` may be omitted
(stays empty and is findable via `?untranslated=true`) and `PartOfSpeech` may be
omitted (default PartOfSpeech.Other). "Complex" additionally fills in
noun/verb/base form/audio; missing details can be supplied later via PATCH.
`Tags` (names) are linked create-if-missing. `TranslationAlternatives` declares further
equally valid translations – equivalence is never derived from two entries sharing a word (those are
homonyms).

CreatorProfileMatch.description:
A match of the profile search for a child. Score is computed deterministically
(a series match weighs heaviest), Reasons names the reasons in plain text –
so a console or a UI can explain the choice instead of showing a bare number.

CreatorProfileResponse.description:
A creator profile including its own permission view. `IsOwn` says whether the calling account
may change the profile; `DefaultTypes` are the preferred exercise types (keys from the type manifest).

Currency.description: The app's two currencies. Currency.Coins ("coins") buys real-world supervisor offers, Currency.Gems buys cosmetic/playful things (skins, future game features). Allowed values: Coins, Gems.

Dashboard.description: The daily overview across all children of a supervisor.

DayOfWeek.description: Allowed values: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.

DayOverview.description: Daily rollup of a study plan across its positions.

DecodedSentence.description: A decoded sentence: original + natural translation + the word-for-word tuples.

DecodedWord.description:
A decoded word of the output: LearningWord in the learning language → literal gloss
Gloss. Gloss/VocabularyId/Self
are `null` if the word is not (yet) in the vocabulary store. Candidates is only

DecodePreviewInput.description: Input for the stateless preview: languages + the sentence to decode along with its translation.

EntryResponse.description: A timetable entry: subject on a weekday.

minWords.description: Minimum length in words (empty = no lower bound).

maxWords.description: Maximum length in words (empty = no upper bound).

ExerciseCheckMode.description:

grantCount.description:
How many explicit permissions hang on it. After withdrawing, this is the circle that can still
assign it – at `1` (only the owner themselves) it is practically out of circulation.

ExerciseSharingResponse.description: The publication status of an exercise after toggling.

ExerciseSummary.description:
Lean hit row of the exercise search (child-neutral catalog). `AuthorAdultId`/`AuthorName` carry the
attribution of the shared library (`null` = seeded system exercise); `IsOwn` = the requesting supervisor
may change/delete the exercise.

type.description: Exercise type key (authoring catalog, = `IExerciseType.Key` and the value of `Exercise.Type`).

renderer.description: Id of the frontend component; multiple types may share one renderer (e.g. Arithmetic + ArithmeticDrill → `arithmetic`).

schemaVersion.description: Version of the type schema. Deliberately ONLY here (not on the entities) – branch point for later incompatible changes.

authoringRoute.description: Route segment of the creator's CRUD under `.../creator/subjects/{subjectId}/chapters/{chapterId}/{AuthoringRoute}`.

playRoute.description: Only for ExerciseCheckMode.StudyPlanTest: segment under `study-plans/{planId}/positions/{positionId}/{PlayRoute}`; otherwise `null`.

oneOf.description: Only for ExerciseCheckMode.StudyPlanTest: learning family for renderer/compatibility; otherwise `null`.

capabilities.description: Type capabilities that a renderer can react to (e.g. `wordBank`, `audio`, `letterHints`).

ExerciseTypeManifest.description:
Self-description of an exercise type: the bridge between the authoring catalog (`IExerciseType`),
typical learning family (LearningMethod), play route, and frontend renderer. The frontend
reads the manifest list once and wires up routing, checking, and display generically; the
actual render component remains hand-built per string ExerciseTypeManifest.Renderer (the play view reveals
a different amount depending on the Leitner box – that cannot be generated generically from JSON).

Gap.description:
A gap. If VocabKey is set, the solution comes from the vocabulary store
(the entry's word), centrally maintainable; the inline Answer remains a fallback for
gaps without a store reference. This allows building a cloze from the maintained vocabulary.

Gender.description:
Gender of the child (purely descriptive). Part of the exercise-independent profile; a later
            study plan generator uses it at most for the language of address, never for filtering the material.

Allowed values: None, Male, Female, Diverse.

GeneratedDrill.description: A freshly generated problem set for a drill exercise.

GeneratedProblem.description: A generated arithmetic expression together with its solution.

GivenAnswer.description: An answer submitted by the child, positional (index in the respective item list).

GoalCadence.description:
Target cadence of a study plan position: at what interval it must be fulfilled.

Allowed values: None, Daily, Weekly.

instruction.description: Optional instruction covering all tasks (e.g. "Put the verb in the correct form").

tasks.description: The individual tasks – the graded content atoms of the exercise.

prompt.description: The task statement, usually with a gap ("He ___ (to feed) the horse").

ruleHint.description: Optional rule hint that may be shown after the answer.

GrantPermission.description:
RWX permission that an owner grants to an individual creator on an exercise. Hierarchy
GrantPermission.Owner ⊃ GrantPermission.Write ⊃ GrantPermission.Execute: an owner may additionally delete,
toggle `Exercise.ExecutePublic`, and grant/revoke permissions themselves. Read is deliberately
not part of the model – the catalog remains readable for everyone (shared library).

Allowed values: Owner, Write, Execute.

GrantResponse.description: A permission granted to a creator.

HeartbeatDto.description: Reports (active) practice seconds; the server caps them per heartbeat (anti time-cheat).

HistoryResponse.description: A logged answer event from the item history.

InterestFacet.description: Facet of an interest tag. It groups the taxonomy by domain without splitting it: topic (InterestFacet.Franchise, InterestFacet.Sport …) and InterestFacet.Style deliberately live in the same table because they behave identically during image selection – only the weighting differs. Extensions are purely additive. Allowed values: Other, Franchise, Sport, Animal, Vehicle, Music, Hobby, Nature, Style.

InterestTagResponse.description:
A tag of the taxonomy including usage counts on both sides: `MediaCount` counts the
assets carrying it, `ChildCount` the children who list it as a like/dislike. `Slug`
is the stable reference name (lowercase, no diacritics), `Facet` distinguishes theme from
presentation style, `Synonyms` holds alternative spellings against duplicates from free text.

InventoryItemDto.description:
An entry in the child's aggregated inventory. `ShopArticleId` is `null` if the
article was deleted after purchase – title and unit then come from the snapshot on the
inventory (as with ActivationRequestDto). Such an entry can no longer be activated:
activation is addressed via the article id.

ItemOutcome.description: Evaluation of a single exam question – here the solution is disclosed.

ItemProgressResponse.description: Learning progress of a child on an item (front/back from the store, canonically word → translation).

ItemReport.description: Report row for a single content item.

ItemResultDto.description: A single result within the completed attempt.

ItemScope.description:
Selection scope of a position's content from the exercise pool.

Allowed values: All, New, Old.

KeyResultMetric.description: Metric by which a `KeyResult` is measured. Deliberately only trick-proof quantities: the outcome-/Leitner-based ones (KeyResultMetric.AvgMastery/KeyResultMetric.MasteredPercent/KeyResultMetric.MaxWeakItems, from `MasteryRollup`) and the class test grade entered by the supervisor (KeyResultMetric.ClassTestGrade). Pure activity counters (minutes/repetitions) are deliberately missing – they reward repeating rather than proficiency and would be farmable. The coverage-based "Coverage" (value 1 of the former `LearnGoalMetric`) is deliberately missing here: it already rises from merely seeing vocabulary – it was the only thing the dropped learning-goal level added, and a farmable one at that. Allowed values: AvgMastery, MasteredPercent, MaxWeakItems, ClassTestGrade.

KeyResultResponse.description: Evaluated key result of an objective.

KlassenarbeitDetail.description: Class test with the directly assigned exercises.

KlassenarbeitStatus.description:
Status of a class test in its lifecycle.

Allowed values: Planned, Written, Cancelled.

items.description: The entries to be named – the graded content atoms of the exercise.

ListConfig.description:
A list to be memorized (e.g. "the 16 German states"). By default, grading only checks
whether the entries were named – order only counts if bool ListConfig.Ordered is set.

audioUrl.description: URL / reference to the audio file.

transcript.description: Optional full transcript of the recording – for the creator only, never for the child (anti-cheat).

questions.description: Questions about the recording – they are the graded content atoms of the exercise.

ListeningConfig.description: Listening comprehension: audio source + comprehension questions.

ListEntry.description: A list entry; Alternatives allows acceptable synonyms/spellings.

role.description: Primary tier for UI routing: `Supervisor`, `Creator`, or `Student`. Ranked in this order – a father holds Creator and Supervisor and belongs in the supervision view, a teacher only holds Creator and belongs in the workshop. The token itself carries all roles of the account; this field only says where the UI should start.

id.description: Domain id of the logged-in profile (adult or child id; account id for account login).

LoginResponse.description: Response of all login endpoints: JWT plus primary tier for UI routing.

LookupRequest.description: Request for the existence check: words (for text extraction) and/or keys (for ref validation).

LookupResponse.description: Response of the existence check: one result per word plus the set of existing keys.

LookupResult.description: Hit per requested word incl. already existing store entries.

MasteryRollup.description: Aggregated learning progress across a set of vocabulary items (same shape at every level).

pairs.description: The pairs to be matched – the graded content atoms of the exercise.

MediaAssetResponse.description:
An asset of the media store including its resolutions and tags. `Description` is at the same time
the alt text for accessibility, `Rating` the suitability (selection never returns an asset
above the child's clearance), `Placeholder` color/blur hash for smooth lazy-loading, and
`Tags` the slugs of the linked interest/style tags.

MediaKind.description:
Media kind of an asset. Today only images are delivered; the store is deliberately open-ended.

Allowed values: Image, Audio, Video.

MediaLinkResponse.description:
An image assignment including the assigned asset (the list should be renderable without an extra fetch).
`Weight` is the editorial rank and only decides ties in the interest score.

MediaOrigin.description:
Origin of an asset – makes generated and third-party content distinguishable in the catalog.

Allowed values: Unknown, Upload, Stock, Generated.

MediaPurpose.description: Semantic delivery slot of a variant. The client asks for the purpose, not for pixel dimensions – this keeps the resolution policy changeable server-side without breaking the contract. Allowed values: Thumb, Card, Full, Hero.

MediaUsage.description:
Where an asset is assigned – the reverse direction of the assignment. `Carrier` is
`vocabulary` | `item` | `exercise`, `Label` a readable designation of the carrier.

MediaVariantResponse.description: A resolution/format of an asset – addressed via its semantic purpose.

accountId.description: Account id (subject of the token); `null` for a legacy token without `aid`.

role.description: Primary tier for routing – see LoginResponse.

roles.description: All roles of the token. For a teacher account, exactly `["Creator"]`.

adultId.description: Domain id of the adult (Creator/Supervisor), otherwise `null`.

childId.description: Domain id of the child (Student), otherwise `null`.

MeResponse.description: The caller's own identity from the token (`GET auth/me`) – account, all roles, and the domain ids.

MissionDto.description: A mission of the child, defined by the supervisor.

MissionPeriod.description:
Period over which a mission counts and renews.

Allowed values: Daily, Weekly, OneOff.

MissionStatus.description: Status of a mission from the child's perspective: target, current value, completed?

MyActivationResponse.description: The child's own activation request from their perspective.

MyInventoryItemResponse.description:
An entry in the child's aggregated inventory: article type → total quantity. `ShopArticleId` is
`null` if the article was deleted after purchase; title and unit then come from the
snapshot on the inventory. What was paid for remains visible – the child just can no longer redeem it,
because activation is addressed via the article id.

MyPointsEntryResponse.description: A single points ledger entry (credit positive, deduction negative) with category.

MyShopPurchaseResponse.description: The child's own purchase ledger entry in their cashbook.

NextResponse.description: The next card in learn mode (or `Done`), server-driven via the session cursor.

article.description: Definite article in the target language (e.g. "der", "die", "das").

oneOf.description: Grammatical gender in the target language.

plural.description: Plural form in the target language (e.g. "die Pferde").

ObjectiveKind.description: Kind of an `Objective` – determines the tone and currency of the reward. ObjectiveKind.Committed is a binding goal (reward in 🪙 coins = real-world privileges); ObjectiveKind.Stretch is a "stretch goal" (reward in 💎 gems = cosmetic). Deliberately, there is no penalty on objectives – the "stick" lives solely on the mandatory goal of the `PlanPosition` (see `PenaltyCoins`). Allowed values: Committed, Stretch.

ObjectiveResponse.description: Evaluated objective incl. key results and roll-up (status `open`/`achieved`/`overdue`).

OverviewResponse.description: Daily mission: the plan overview plus today's rollup over its positions.

PartOfSpeech.description:
Part of speech of a store vocabulary item. Determines which additional details make sense
(NounInfo for nouns, VerbInfo for verbs) and is a filter criterion
in the vocabulary store. PartOfSpeech.Other is the default when the author specifies nothing.

Allowed values: Noun, Verb, Adjective, Adverb, Pronoun, Preposition, Conjunction, Article, Numeral, Interjection, Phrase, Other.

isPlayable.description: Server-authoritative affordance: whether this is the one currently playable plan of the child (active and within its run today). For the student, only this one is ever visible; for the supervisor, among several plans it shows the one the student can currently play – without reimplementing the rule on the client.

PlanResponse.description: A study plan container of a child.

PlanUsage.description: A study plan in which an exercise is used as a position.

PlayMode.description: Play mode of an exercise session. PlayMode.Info = free practice: content all in a row, the frontend drives the iteration, and no learning feedback flows (no grading/points/Leitner, doesn't count toward the goal). PlayMode.Lern = server-driven: the server holds the cursor + frozen order and grades. Allowed values: Info, Lern.

PointKind.description:
Category of a points ledger entry – makes bonuses evaluable/cappable (e.g. "how many points
came from combo vs. time of day?"). PointKind.Base is the default for legacy entries.

Allowed values: Base, Manual, Combo, Speed, Mission, Achievement, SkinPurchase, Goal, ShopCoins, ShopGems, ManualGems, GoalPenalty, ObjectiveCoins, ObjectiveGems.

currency.description: Target currency of the entry (default coins).

PointsEntryDto.description: Manual supervisor ledger entry: positive amount = credit/gift, negative = deduct. Via the currency, the supervisor can also gift gems alongside coins (reward outside the app, debt forgiveness).

PointsEntryResponse.description: A points ledger entry of the child.

studyPlanId.description: Study plan the position belongs to.

exerciseId.description: The referenced catalog exercise. Immutable: Leitner progress is anchored to it via item indices; swapping it would redirect that progress onto unrelated content.

exerciseTitle.description: Title of the exercise – included so a list is readable without a second round trip.

exerciseType.description: Type key of the exercise (a value from the type manifest).

stage.description: Query form of the final test; `null` = default of the exercise or the method.

itemCount.description: How many items per run; `null` = all.

scope.description: Which part of the content is played (see ItemScope).

cadence.description:
Goal cadence (see GoalCadence). `None` = free practice that does not count toward
the mandatory goal – and therefore cannot trigger a penalty either.

orderStrategy.description: Play-out order (see PracticeOrder); it is frozen at the start of a session/test.

goalThreshold.description: Passing threshold of the final test in percent of correct answers; `null` = 80%. The unit applies to all testable exercise types – including catalog checks, since a position's goal is always measured by a passed position test. Unused for pure content exercises.

requireTypedTest.description: Only typed, objectively checkable stages in the final test – no self-assessment.

useLeitner.description: Leitner box with review scheduling instead of a single simple pass.

maxBox.description: Highest Leitner box; an item there counts as mastered (default 5).

boxIntervalDays.description: Review interval in days per box; `null` = method default.

stageSchedule.description: Schedule of which query form applies at which box; `null` = method default.

pointsGoalMet.description: Points when the period's goal is met.

penaltyCoins.description: Coin penalty for a missed mandatory goal (the "stick"); `0` = pure reward. Only booked for completed periods, and may drive the balance negative.

newContentPoints.description: Points for a piece of content introduced for the first time.

comboThreshold.description: How many correct answers in a row trigger the combo bonus.

speedThresholdSeconds.description: Up to how many seconds an answer counts as "fast"; `0` = off.

PositionResponse.description: A position in the study plan: the referenced exercise together with its own goal, points, stage, and Leitner settings.

PositionStatus.description: Status of a single position for one day – enough for the student client to render the right action.

PracticeCard.description: A practice card – deliberately WITHOUT the solution, except at display/self-assessment stages that reveal the solution by design (the server grades, never the frontend). `ImageUrl`/`ImageAlt` carry the image selected for this child; they are only set at stages where a motif cannot give away the solution, and are absent otherwise.

PracticeOrder.description: Ordering strategy in which the server plays out a position's (due) content. The order is materialized (frozen) once at the start of the session/test, so it doesn't shift mid-run when boxes change due to answers. Allowed values: WeakestFirst, Serial, Random, NewestWeighted.

PracticeResponse.description: Exercises relevant to a class test for targeted practice (days until the date, inclusive).

PreviewAnswer.description: An answer from the supervisor: typed (GivenAnswer) or self-assessment (WasKnown).

PreviewCheckDto.description:
Body of the test-mode check: the submitted answers and – if toggled – the query form.
Deliberately not named `CheckDto`: that name is used by the stateless catalog check of the exercise type.

PreviewData.description:
The playable state of an exercise in test mode: type, chosen stage, whether typed, the problems and
– for trying out – the query forms toggleable for this exercise type (IReadOnlyList<StageOption> PreviewData.Stages).

PreviewItem.description:
A problem presented in test mode. `Reveal` carries the revealed solution for self-assessment
(`null` for typed stages); `AnswerLength` is only set for vocabulary letter boxes.

PreviewItemOutcome.description: Individual evaluation including the expected solution (in test mode the solution is always disclosed).

PreviewResult.description: Overall result of a test-mode run.

ProfileRole.description:
The three domain tiers as a role – independent of login.

Allowed values: Creator, Supervisor, Student.

ProgressDay.description: One day in the history (for the supervisor's evaluation).

ProgressMetric.description:
Measurable quantity of a child's learning activity – shared basis for missions and awards.
All values are computed server-side from the existing tables (no client trust).

Allowed values: NewWords, CorrectReviews, TestsPassed, MinutesPracticed, DaysComplete, StreakDays.

ProgressResponse.description: Day-by-day progress over the entire run (completed days, goals reached, points).

Question.description: Question with optional answer choices (empty = free text).

questions.description: Questions about the text – they are the graded content atoms of the exercise.

RefsFromTagsDto.description: Selecting vocabulary by tag instead of a manual reference list.

RemarkCategory.description:
Classification of a remark. RemarkCategory.Unspecified is the common case when capturing it: categorizing
while testing costs more time than it's worth – the follow-up skill derives the classification from
the text afterward.

Allowed values: Unspecified, Bug, Ui, Code, Content, Idea, Question.

RemarkCommentAuthor.description:
Origin of a contribution in a remark's history.
            Deliberately a dedicated field and not derived from the author account: Claude writes via the
skill using the human's token, so both contributions would carry the same account. A rule hinges on
this distinction, though – a RemarkCommentAuthor.Human contribution reopens a done remark, while an
RemarkCommentAuthor.Assistant contribution leaves the state untouched.

Allowed values: Human, Assistant.

authorAccountId.description: Account of the writer, if known.

isOwn.description: Whether the comment originates from the requesting account – only own comments can be deleted.

RemarkCommentDto.description:
A comment in the thread of a remark. Complements string? RemarkDto.Answer (the one authoritative
resolution) rather than replacing it: analysis, follow-up question, and implementation note sit
side by side instead of overwriting one another.

childId.description: Child that was selected at capture time.

exerciseId.description: Exercise that was open at capture time.

studyPlanId.description: Study plan that was open at capture time.

planPositionId.description: Position that was open at capture time.

contextJson.description: State snapshot (filter, selection, open modal) as raw JSON – only IDs and filter values, never loaded entities.

recentErrorsJson.description: Ring buffer of the most recent errors as raw JSON. Metadata only (method, path, status, error `code`, timestamp) – no bodies, headers, or tokens: the login request carries the PIN in the body.

RemarkContextDto.description:
The context snapshot at the time of capture – the real value of a remark.
The widget fills it in automatically; the human only types the text.

id.description: The "log id" shown to the human – the key for "answer question 123".

parentRemarkId.description: Predecessor remark, if this one arose from an answer.

accountId.description: Account of the person who captured it.

authorRole.description: Role at the time of capture.

isOwn.description: Whether the remark originates from the requesting account – the widget shows only its own.

commentCount.description:
Number of comments in the thread. Kept on the remark so the list and widget can show "3 comments"
without reloading the thread for every row.

RemarkDto.description: A remark, as delivered by the API.

RemarkStatus.description:
Processing state of a remark. Deliberately lean: no assignment, no milestones – four states
are enough so the follow-up skill doesn't present the same remarks again on every run.

Allowed values: Open, Planned, Done, Rejected.

RepeatResponse.description: Exercises that should be repeated because of poorly graded class tests.

Report.description: Report of a position including headline metrics (introduced/mastered).

ReshuffleMediaDto.description:
"Different picture": rejects the currently chosen image of a carrier and draws a new one. Exactly one of
the two fields must be set – ExerciseItemId if the exercise carries its own
mapping, otherwise VocabularyId for the word itself (then the new pick applies everywhere).

ReviewDto.description:
The child's answer to a practice card. ItemIndex addresses the content atom
in the exercise. Typed stages supply GivenAnswer, display/self-assessment
stages supply WasKnown. The server enforces the stage; it grades – never the frontend.

ReviewOutcome.description:
Result of a Leitner review (graded server-side) incl. bonuses for feedback. PracticeCard? ReviewOutcome.Next
carries the next card directly in learn mode (no separate roundtrip needed); bool ReviewOutcome.Done signals
the end of the run. For cards that are not graded (not due / already graded today / not Leitner-based),
the points fields are 0, but grading and cursor still advance.

maxScore.description: Maximum score this criterion can achieve.

RubricCriterion.description: A grading criterion of an essay.

SchoolTypes.description:
School types for which an exercise is suitable. A `[Flags]` enum so that an exercise
can be assigned to multiple school types (e.g. Realschule | Gymnasium).
SchoolTypes.None means "for all school types" (no filter exclusion).

Allowed values: None, Grundschule, Hauptschule, Realschule, Gymnasium, Gesamtschule, Berufsschule.

SeriesUnitResponse.description:
A unit of the series including volume. `Topics`, `Grammar` and `VocabularyNotes` are the
material an AI creator must know so as not to invent the unit.

SessionResponse.description: A running or finished practice session on a position.

SetChildInterestsDto.description:
Replaces the child's interests entirely with the given list (empty list = remove all).
Deliberately a full replacement rather than additive, because the UI edits the set as a whole.

SetChildInterestWeightDto.description: Sets/changes the weight of a single tag (upsert).

executePublic.description: `true` = any creator may assign it to a child. `false` = withdrawn: only whoever holds an explicit permission on the exercise (owner/write/execute) can still make new assignments. What withdrawing does not do: touch running study plans. The check applies when assigning, not when playing – a child learning the exercise today keeps learning it. That is exactly why this is the way to take material out of circulation, and not deletion (which a used exercise refuses anyway).

SetExerciseSharingDto.description: Input for publishing or withdrawing an exercise – the counter-move to publishing.

ShopArticleDto.description: A basic catalog article of the supervisor: the kind of article (unit + category).

ShopListingDto.description: A listing for an article: price in both currencies, stock, and refill rule.

ShopListingResponse.description: A purchasable offer from the family shop from the child's perspective (listing level).

canCancel.description: May the supervisor cancel and refund this purchase now?

ShopPurchaseDto.description: A historical purchase entry of the child.

ShopPurchaseStatus.description:
State of a historical shop purchase entry.

Allowed values: Owned, Cancelled.

ShopRefillKind.description:
Automatic restock rule for a shop listing (`ShopListing`).

Allowed values: None, Once, Daily, TwiceDaily, Weekly.

ShopViewResponse.description: The child's shop view: wallet, purchasable offers, aggregated inventory and purchase history.

SkinStateResponse.description: Skin state of the child: current gem balance, equipped and unlocked skins.

StageOption.description: A query form that can be switched in test mode (stage value + display label).

StageStep.description: A step in the stage schedule: from day `DayNumber` (1-based) onward, stage `Stage` applies.

StartPracticeDto.description:
Start payload of a practice session. Mode selects the playback mode (default
PlayMode.Lern = server-driven with cursor; PlayMode.Info = free practice without
feedback). Day only for backfilling (supervisor).

StartTestDto.description: Start payload of the class test. `Day` only for backfilling (supervisor); otherwise today.

SubjectProgressResponse.description: Progress of a subject. Active = contains ≥1 exercise currently assigned (via an active plan).

SubjectResponse.description: A school subject in the shared catalog.

SubmitDto.description: Bulk submission of the test (alternative to individual submission via the `answer` endpoint).

SubmitResponse.description: Overall result of the class test incl. pass threshold.

SuggestedBonus.description:
Bonus system suggested by the exercise author (global on the exercise). Serves only as a template:
when a study plan is created from the exercise, these values are copied ONCE into its bonus fields.
Later changes to the exercise therefore do NOT retroactively affect existing child plans –
the running bonus system remains child-specific and adjustable per study plan (motivation control
per child/exercise). Fields mirror the bonus knobs of the `StudyPlan`.

SupervisorLinkResponse.description: A supervision relationship: which supervisor supervises the student since when.

SupervisorRelation.description:
Kinship role of a supervisor to the student (purely descriptive).

Allowed values: Father, Mother, Grandma, Grandpa, Guardian, Other.

TagExercisesDto.description: Input for tagging exercises with a tag.

TaggedBy.description:
Who made a tagging (for traceability in the dashboard).

Allowed values: Vater, Sohn.

TaggedVocabularyDto.description: Lean vocabulary view for the tag assignment (without the child-neutral store details).

TagMediaDto.description: Links an asset with tags of the shared taxonomy (slugs, create-if-missing).

TagRef.description: A tag in short form, as attached to a class test.

TagResponse.description: Tag in the response incl. count of tagged exercises and vocabulary entries.

TagVocabDto.description: Input for linking a vocabulary entry with tags (create-if-missing via the names).

TagVocabularyDto.description: Input for tagging vocabulary entries with a child-scoped tag.

creatorId.description: Domain id of the creator (login name).

accountId.description: Account id for the account-centric login `auth/login`.

roles.description: The account's roles – for a teacher only`Creator`. Deliberately in the response: the difference to a father account is exactly this list, and it should be visible without a second call.

TeacherAccountResponse.description: The created teacher account. CreatorId is the login name and at the same time the id under which their authorship and their permissions on exercises hang.

TestItem.description: An exam question – without the solution, except at stages that reveal it by design. Deliberately without an image: the exam shows none, and a field that is always null is the kind of silent lie the API otherwise rejects with `unknown_field`.

TestNextResponse.description: The next exam question (or `Done`), server-driven via the attempt cursor – without the solution.

TextbookResponse.description:
A textbook used by the child, together with its current chapter. `SeriesId`/`CurrentUnitId`
are the cataloged form of title and chapter: only through them does the profile matching find the
creator who knows this work.

TextbookSeriesResponse.description:
A textbook series ("Access") including its own permission view. `Slug` is the normalized, globally
unique and immutable key of the series, `IsOwn` says whether the calling account may
change it, `UnitCount` counts the stored units across all volumes.

sourceLang.description: Source language as a language code (e.g. "en").

targetLang.description: Target language as a language code (e.g. "de").

items.description: The sentence pairs – the graded content atoms of the exercise.

TranslationItem.description:
A translation pair. VocabularyId refers to the associated store entry
(automatically created on save); Self is the derived, read-only populated link.

UnitType.description:
Unit of measurement of the item – determines how quantities are displayed in the inventory and upon activation.

Allowed values: Stueck, Minute, Stunde, Gramm, Mal.

UpdateAchievementDto.description: Partial change to an award; the metric is immutable.

UpdateAdultDto.description: Only fields that are set are changed.

UpdateCategoryDto.description: Partial change to a category; empty fields remain unchanged.

UpdateChapterDto.description: Partial change to a chapter; empty fields remain unchanged.

UpdateChildDto.description: Partial change to a child; omitted fields stay unchanged. `null` means "not specified" and therefore cannot clear anything – that is what the `Clear…` switches are for (cf. `ClearGrade` on the class test): `ClearBirthYear` removes the birth year, `ClearGrade` the grade level (the child then drops out of grade filters).

UpdateClassTestDto.description: Partial change – among other things, recording a grade and setting status. `ClearGrade` deletes the grade.

UpdateClozeDto.description:
Partial change to a cloze: `null` means "not specified" (the value remains).
The two optional contents are therefore cleared via bool UpdateClozeDto.ClearTranslation resp.
bool UpdateClozeDto.ClearWordBank – a field cleared in a form would arrive as `null` and would
otherwise be indistinguishable from "unchanged".

UpdateCreatorProfileDto.description:
Partial change to a profile; omitted fields remain unchanged.
            A null means "not specified" in a PATCH – so it cannot clear a field.
The Clear… switches (like ClearGrade on the class test) exist for that: only with them
can a profile become subject-neutral, series-independent, or grade-open again.

UpdateInterestTagDto.description: Only fields that are set are changed; `Synonyms` replaces the list entirely.

UpdateKeyResultRequest.description: Partial update of a key result: metric/target value/title (scope stays fixed).

UpdateMediaAssetDto.description: Only fields that are set are changed; `Tags` are appended (not replaced).

UpdateMediaLinkDto.description: Changes the editorial rank of an existing assignment.

UpdateMediaVariantDto.description: Only fields that are set are changed.

UpdateMissionDto.description: Partial change to a mission; metric and period are immutable.

name.description: New display name; also appears as the author on the account's own exercises.

email.description: New email. Must be unique account-wide.

clearEmail.description: Remove the email. Wins over Email if both are sent.

pin.description:
New login PIN (will be hashed). Empty string = remove the PIN, so an account can
            be deliberately deactivated; `null` = unchanged.

UpdateMyAccountDto.description: Self-service management of the caller's own account (`PATCH auth/me`) – for every adult role, including a teacher account that has no access to the supervisor endpoints. PATCH semantics:null means "not specified" (the value stays). Email is the only clearable field and needs bool UpdateMyAccountDto.ClearEmail for that – without the switch, a form with an empty field would report "saved" while the old address stayed in place.

UpdateObjectiveRequest.description: Partial update of an objective: only the fields that are set change.

UpdatePlanDto.description: Partial change to the container. int? UpdatePlanDto.ChildId reassigns the plan to another of the caller's own children.

stage.description: Query form of the final test.

oneOf.description: Which part of the content (see ItemScope).

goalThreshold.description: Passing threshold in percent (see PositionResponse); `null` = not specified.

requireTypedTest.description: Only typed stages in the final test.

useLeitner.description: Leitner box instead of a single simple pass.

pointsGoalMet.description: Points when the goal is met.

penaltyCoins.description: Coin penalty for a missed mandatory goal.

UpdatePositionDto.description:
Partial change to the overrides/goals/points. The referenced exercise is immutable
(progress indices).
PATCH semantics:null means "not specified" for every field – the previous
value stays. It does not mean "reset to default"; that would need its own
Clear switch, which this DTO deliberately does not have.

answer.description: The answer (written back by the skill); retained even at RemarkStatus.Planned.

answeredBy.description: Who answered, e.g. `claude-code`. Only takes effect together with Answer.

clearAnswer.description: Clear the answer together with its timestamp/author.

clearParent.description: Clear the reference to the parent remark.

UpdateRemarkDto.description: Change a remark. PATCH semantics: `null` means "not specified" (the value stays), not "clear" – that is what the explicit `Clear…` switches are for.

UpdateSeriesUnitDto.description: Partial change to a unit; omitted fields remain unchanged.

UpdateShopArticleDto.description: Partial change to a catalog article; omitted fields stay unchanged.

UpdateShopListingDto.description: Partial change to a listing; omitted fields stay unchanged.

UpdateSubjectDto.description: Partial change to a subject; empty fields remain unchanged.

UpdateTagDto.description: Partial change to a tag; empty fields remain unchanged.

UpdateTextbookDto.description: Partial change to a textbook; omitted fields stay unchanged.

UpdateTextbookSeriesDto.description: Partial change to a series; omitted fields remain unchanged. The slug stays fixed.

UpdateVocabTagDto.description: Partial change to a vocabulary tag; empty fields remain unchanged.

UpdateVocabularyDto.description:
Only fields that are set are changed. BaseFormKey = "" removes the link (and its label); tags are
appended (not replaced). `null` means "not specified" (the value remains), so the alternatives are
dropped via bool UpdateVocabularyDto.ClearTranslationAlternatives – a list emptied in a form would arrive as
`null` and would otherwise be indistinguishable from "unchanged". An explicitly empty list clears
them too; the switch exists for the case the client cannot tell the two apart.

plans.description: Study plans of own children in which the exercise is used as a position.

classTests.description: Class tests of own children (assigned directly or via a tag).

otherLearnersCount.description: How many different children use the exercise whom the caller does not supervise – just the number, without names. Two reasons: * Without it the lists report "nowhere" while deletion fails with 409 exercise_in_use – a contradiction the author cannot resolve (remark 14). * For a creator without own children (a teacher, or an AI creator app), both lists are permanently empty. This number is then not the footnote but the only answer to their actual question: is my material being used?Children are counted, not usage sites: three positions in the same child's plans are one user. The basis is the FK-relevant usages that also block deletion – a class test only collected via a tag does not prevent it and is therefore not counted.

UsageResponse.description: Where an exercise is used. IReadOnlyList<PlanUsage> UsageResponse.Plans and IReadOnlyList<ClassTestUsage> UsageResponse.ClassTests only name resources of the caller's own children – other supervisors' children must not show up here.

isBaseForm.description: true = base form (infinitive), false = inflected form.

infinitive.description: Base form this form belongs to (e.g. "to go" for "went").

partOfSpeech.description: Part of speech (helps distinguish identical spellings).

VocabCandidate.description: An interchangeable vocabulary candidate for a word (several for homonyms).

VocabItem.description: Inline vocabulary item – the same input shape as the item endpoint (`VocabItemInput`): word via VocabularyId (existing store entry; Front/Back then come from the store) or inline via Front/Back (created/found in the store on save). Both are therefore optional; an item needs either the VocabularyId or Front and Back. Self is the derived, read-only populated HATEOAS link.

VocabItemInput.description:
Creating/changing an item: either via VocabularyId (existing store vocabulary) or inline
via Front/Back (created/found in the store). Hint
empty = delete, set = overwrite; on PATCH every omitted field remains unchanged.

front.description: Word in the learning language (from the store).

hint.description: Exercise-local hint; overrides the derived store hint.

_self.description: HATEOAS link to the item itself.

vocabulary.description: HATEOAS link to the store entry.

VocabItemResponse.description: A single vocabulary pair of the exercise. Front/back come from the linked store entry.

VocabTagResponse.description: Child-neutral vocabulary tag incl. count of linked vocabulary entries.

sourceLang.description: Language code of the source language (e.g. "en"); needed to create inline List<VocabItem> VocabularyConfig.Items in the store.

targetLang.description: Language code of the target language (e.g. "de"); needed to create inline List<VocabItem> VocabularyConfig.Items in the store.

refs.description: References to vocabulary store entries (by ID; the response adds the link).

items.description: Inline vocabulary items; without int? VocabItem.VocabularyId they are automatically created in the store on save.

VocabularyConfig.description:
Vocabulary exercise. References entries of the vocabulary store via List<VocabRef>? VocabularyConfig.Refs (by int VocabRef.VocabularyId),
so the same vocabulary item can be linked across multiple exercises and maintained centrally. Inline List<VocabItem> VocabularyConfig.Items
without their own int? VocabItem.VocabularyId are automatically created in the store and linked on save –
this guarantees every used vocabulary item lives in the store. string VocabularyConfig.SourceLang/string VocabularyConfig.TargetLang are
needed for this (the store key is formed from language + word + translation).

VocabularyResponse.description:
A store entry with all lexical details and the linked tag names.
`TranslationAlternatives` are further translations that count as equally correct for
`Translation` when answering "word → ?".

VocabUsage.description: An exercise that references this vocabulary entry (vocabulary refs resp. cloze gap).

WalletResponse.description: Account balance (wallet) of the child per currency. The ledger entries are under `points/entries`.

WordMasteryResponse.description: Aggregated word mastery status across all exercises that use this store word.

WordOverride.description:
Correction of a single word. VocabularyId set → the gloss follows this card
(correct meaning for homonyms). Only Gloss set → free gloss without a card. Both
empty → remove gloss (word stays undecoded).

WordPair.description:
A word tuple of the decoding: LearningWord of the language being learned → literal native-language
gloss Gloss. Gloss/VocabularyId are `null` if
the word is not (yet) in the vocabulary store and no manual gloss was set. WordId
is unique exercise-wide (see int BirkenbihlConfig.NextWordId).
